calls.summary: The team discussed strategies to simplify release rules by merging overlapping options, integrating safe rollout concepts with ramping strategies, and enhancing user understanding without compromising existing configurations. They also emphasized implementing distinct monitoring metrics tailored to different rollout phases and centralizing monitoring frequency for better resource management. The plan includes a focus on maintaining clear communication regarding monitoring status, particularly when rollout coverage exceeds 50%. Additionally, the rollout system will rely on REST APIs for external metric integration, and a potential release postponement to early/mid May was proposed to ensure a high-quality rollout experience while managing ongoing feature development.
calls.keywords: safe rollout, ramp scheduling, guardrail metrics, rollout monitoring, feature flag lifecycle, rollback automation

calls.summary: The team discussed integrating all SDK user attributes into the contextual bandit callback to enhance flexibility in targeting and logging. They agreed that this would aid in debugging and allow for more personalized user experiences, despite the potential for large attribute sets. A third argument will be added to the callback signature to facilitate the mapping of attributes, ensuring ease of access during evaluations. Additionally, direct SQL column-to-attribute mapping was emphasized to streamline the data warehouse process, alongside the importance of dual validation for both SDK attributes and SQL queries. The team planned to hold twice-weekly meetings to coordinate efforts effectively and address any blockers.
calls.keywords: Contextual Bandit, SDK Callback, Attribute Mapping, Data Warehouse, SQL Query, Personalization Payload

calls.summary: The team is dedicated to creating a minimum viable product (MVP) for Contextual Bandits, emphasizing essential features while minimizing initial UI resources. They are considering an API-first approach to facilitate early feedback from key clients like Anthropic and Sony, which would allow programmatic interaction without an extensive UI. The MVP will focus on core bandit mechanics and data models, with early releases potentially using beta SDK versions for feedback collection. Separation from existing code aims to avoid technical debt, while programmatic control is balanced with UI needs. The development will adopt iterative strategies with feature flags and beta releases to ensure product-market fit and manage rollout risks effectively.

calls.title: teresa@growthbook.io - Thu, 30 Apr 2026 14:01:10 PDT - Untitled
calls.summary: The team is developing a new contextual bandit data model aimed at managing context expansion and performance constraints. Teresa has created a flattened model to circumvent MongoDB's 16MB document size limit and is testing it using hard-coded API inputs. Meanwhile, Luke Sonnet emphasized the need to move existing experiment assignment queries into separate collections for better permissions and management, with migration expected within 1-2 months. The team decided to exclude holdout groups from the initial version of the contextual bandit experiment to expedite its rollout, focusing on core functionality first. Luke Smith is reviewing advanced statistical methods for arm selection and planning to enhance decisions through academic insights. Asynchronous communication will be used for feedback on the data model before the next meeting.
calls.keywords: contextual bandit, data model, experiment queries, holdout arm, permission scoping, multi-armed bandit modeling

calls.summary: The team addressed key updates for table design, focusing on adjusting header font weights, standardizing text colors to Indigo 12, and fixing background colors to ensure visual clarity. Font weight was set to 500 to improve readability, while the consistent application of the Indigo 12 color token aimed to enhance brand coherence. The header background was standardized to white to resolve inconsistencies, and borders set to Slate A5 for subtle separation. Challenges were identified with third-party libraries overwriting styles, requiring strategic customizations. Immediate actions included finalizing color and border updates, with a target to merge the changes shortly.
